messages:
support_jane: FYI, customer `cust-acme` reporting higher p95/p99 for /v1/generate from EU region starting ~09:15 UTC. p95 jumped ~120ms -> ~520ms, p99 ~1.2s. No error rate increase, just latency. Customer on eu-west1.

kevin_oncall: Ack. Can you paste a quick client-side curl timing and any app logs? Also their region header/ingress host? I'll start tracing from edge.

support_jane: Curl from their probe (09:18 UTC):
```
$ curl -w "%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer} %{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
0.090 0.410 0.425
```
They see similar. No 5xx, auth OK. Host header: api.eu.redwood.ai.

kevin_oncall: Thx. @tara_infra can you run edge traceroute + tcpdump on eu-west1 border pop? Looking for extra RTTs during TLS handshake.

tara_infra: Running now. Quick traceroute to client IP shows an unexpected hop to another eu pop before origin:
```
traceroute to 1.2.3.4 (1.2.3.4), 10 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  edge-eu-west1 (10.1.1.1)  2.4 ms  2.0 ms  1.9 ms
 2  anycast-eu-west2 (10.2.2.2)  45.3 ms  44.9 ms  45.1 ms
 3  client-net (1.2.3.4)  46.0 ms  45.8 ms  45.9 ms
```
And tcpdump TLS handshake timing: SYN->SYN/ACK ~2ms, SYN/ACK->TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello round trips appear fine locally, but TLS handshake completion time shows ~300-400ms at the server side (we see delayed ACK from upstream).

alex_net: Looks like GSLB routed traffic through eu-west2 (anycast) causing cross-pop hairpin. We had a mini failover 09:12 UTC for a subset of IPs due to healthcheck jitter; some prefixes got routed to eu-west2 then back. That explains extra ~40ms + TLS overhead.

maria_sre: Is this tied to aggressive healthcheck backoff we rolled last week? If so, we might be oscillating when backend latency spikes for short windows. Suggest temporary mitigation: pin the customer's GSLB answer to eu-west1 (bypass failover) and increase healthcheck dampening for the originating pool.

kevin_oncall: Agreed. I'll pin routes for cust-acme and apply a dampening change. Executing route pin now.

route-bot: /route pin cust-acme -> eu-west1 (initiated by kevin_oncall)
route-bot: pin applied: cust-acme pinned to eu-west1 for 30m (will auto-expire)

kevin_oncall: Also toggled healthcheck backoff from aggressive->conservative for pool eu-ingress-1 (change id hc-2026). This reduces failover sensitivity.

deploy-bot: healthcheck config hc-2026 updated in canary pools (eu-ingress-1).

tara_infra: Re-ran client probe at 09:28 UTC after pin:
```
$ curl -w "%{time_starttransfer} %{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.eu.redwood.ai/v1/generate
0.115 0.160
```
p95 back to ~160ms observed from customer probe. p99 down too.

maria_sre: Good. Follow-ups: 1) revert pin after 30m and monitor global routing stability; 2) audit last week's healthcheck tuning and partially roll back the most aggressive parameters; 3) long-term: add route affinity hints per-tenant to avoid cross-pop hairpin on transient flaps.

support_jane: I'll send update to customer: mitigation applied, latency returning to normal, engineering tracking root cause (healthcheck oscillation -> hairpin).

kevin_oncall: Leaving pin for 30m so we can watch SLOs; will post end-of-incident summary later. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: metrics snapshot: region=eu-west1 p95 09:00-09:10 125ms -> 09:20-09:30 170ms (post-mitigation 160ms). p99 reduced from ~1.2s -> ~220ms.

maria_sre: I'll open a follow-up ticket to revert the aggressive healthcheck change and schedule canary for any future tuning. Ticket: INFRA-8472.

support_jane: Customer updated and satisfied for now. Closing escalation unless it recurs.

kevin_oncall: Thanks team. Postmortem will include evidence of GSLB failover, healthcheck diff, and the route pin timeline.
